keyVerseText: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.
rootMeaning: The Greek verb περιΐστημι (periḯstēmi) derives from the combination of περί (peri), meaning 'around' or 'about,' and ἵστημι (histēmi), meaning 'to stand.' Thus, its root meaning involves the concept of standing or placing oneself all around or surrounding something. This literal sense of encircling or standing near adds depth beyond the English glosses such as 'avoid' or 'shun,' suggesting not only physical proximity but also relational positioning either near or at a distance.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, περιΐστημι is used with a range of meanings including 'stand by,' 'stood round about,' 'shun,' and 'avoid,' occurring four times in total. This variety shows the word’s flexibility to describe both physical standing near others, as well as a deliberate distancing or avoidance. The consistency in these translations reveals a core idea of relational stance—either being present around someone or consciously withdrawing from something or someone.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding περιΐστημι enriches our grasp of relational dynamics in Scripture, highlighting how presence and avoidance both have spiritual significance. The verb’s original meaning of standing around or positioning oneself reflects how believers are called to both stand by one another in faith and shun what is contrary to godliness. It reminds us that faith involves intentional posture—sometimes drawing near to support, other times turning away to avoid sin. This dual aspect underscores the believer’s call to be discerning and purposeful in relationships, reflecting Christ’s example perfectly.
keyVerseReflection: In John 11:42, Jesus refers to 'the people which stand by' (περιΐστημι) as witnesses to His prayer, so that they may believe He was sent by the Father. Here, the word emphasizes the presence of bystanders surrounding the event, reinforcing the reality and public nature of Jesus’ actions. The use of περιΐστημι highlights not only physical proximity but also the relational significance of those who observe and are invited into faith through witnessing Christ’s works.
